claims.claim: US estate tax applies above the $15M exemption (2026)

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026

sources.name: Consortium Legal: Permanent residence as a rentier or pensioner in Central America
sources.says: Dated 16 January 2026. Guatemala: residency "is regulated by Agreement IGM 16-2025"; for those with "legal and verifiable income from abroad", "The minimum income requirement is US$1,250, plus an additional US$300 for each dependent"; submitted to the Guatemalan Migration Institute. Honduras: pensionado "requiring a minimum income of US$1,500 per month"; rentista "the minimum income is US$2,500"; handled by the Ministry of the Interior and Justice.

sources.name: Consortium Legal: Residencia en Honduras
sources.says: Dated 15 November 2021 by its URL. Rentista: "rentas permanentes, lícitas, y estables generadas en el exterior o en el territorio nacional" of at least US$2,500 a month; pensionado: pensions from abroad of at least US$1,500 a month; categories under "artículo veintiuno de la Ley de Migracion y Extranjeria"; the residence "no requiere ser renovada".

sources.name: Rio Times: retire in Honduras as a foreigner (2026)
sources.says: Dated September 22, 2026. Ley de Migración y Extranjería (Decree 208-2003): rentista (art. 23, US$2,500 a month, from abroad or Honduras) and pensionado (art. 24, US$1,500 foreign pension); "the money has to be received through a bank or other institution of the Honduran financial system"; "pensionado and rentista cards are renewed yearly", with a bank certificate at renewal.

claims.note: Also the summary and the why line. "Which portfolio income should meet" is the profile's reading and rides with this.

claims.claim: The island's only public hospital burned down on 19 April 2024

sources.name: Direct Relief: Fire destroyed an island hospital; months later a Honduran free clinic is still bridging the gap
sources.says: Dated October 17, 2024. The April 19 fire destroyed "the only public hospital on the island of Roatán"; a replacement would take about 18 months to build; two privately operated hospitals are still open.

claims.note: Also the summary, drawback and the why line.

claims.claim: Rebuilding was expected to take about 18 months, leaving private hospitals and clinics
claims.oldWording: (rebuilding was expected to take about 18 months), leaving private hospitals and clinics
claims.newWording: its replacement, Hospital Satuyé, has reportedly operated since September 2025 alongside private hospitals and clinics

sources.name: La Prensa: hospital modernisation and primary care
sources.says: Updated 17 December 2025. Health Minister Carla Paredes: the Hospital Satuyé in Roatán "ya fue entregado y se encuentra en funcionamiento"; caption: "Desde septiembre, el Hospital en Roatán opera equipado, con instalaciones modernas y servicios especializados."

sources.name: La Prensa: two new public hospitals will soon open in Roatán
sources.says: Updated 2 June 2025. The permanent public hospital at Loma Linda is being finished by the central government; an emergency hospital at Dixon Cove, 70% built, was due in August, with obstetrics, surgery, intensive care, neonatology, lab, outpatients and emergencies.

sources.name: El Heraldo: measles case at Hospital Satuyé, Roatán
sources.says: Updated 31 May 2026. Health authorities of the Bay Islands asked people who had been at "las instalaciones del Hospital Satuyé" in Roatán on 26 May to be checked; it is described as a "centro asistencial", not as public or private.

sources.name: Direct Relief: Fire destroyed an island hospital; months later a Honduran free clinic is still bridging the gap
sources.says: Dated October 17, 2024. The April 19 fire destroyed "the only public hospital on the island of Roatán"; a replacement would take about 18 months to build; two privately operated hospitals are still open.

also: summary: "the island's only public hospital burned in April 2024" became "hospital care is thin: the public hospital burned in April 2024 and was reportedly replaced only in 2025"
drawback 1 reworded: "Thin hospital care: the public hospital burned in 2024 and was reportedly replaced only in 2025, and serious illness means an evacuation flight"
scores.healthcare stays 1 (Canada, October 2026: facilities "very limited", major procedures may need evacuation)
claims.rankFlag: Roatán (pick 59): the why says "the island's public hospital burned in 2024, serious cases fly out". Both halves are still true (Canada still advises evacuation for major procedures), but the island has had a public hospital again since September 2025 by the health minister's account, so the why reads as if the gap were current. No change proposed; the healthcare score stays 1.
claims.note: The 18-month estimate was right (Direct Relief, 2024) and is now moot. The minister's statement is reported by a newspaper; no Health Secretariat page was read, and the pages do not say plainly that Satuyé is the Loma Linda or the Dixon Cove building, hence "reportedly".
